newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmaker presses for NAFTA access for Chile.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmaker presses for NAFTA access for Chile.

text.p: The United States should move quickly to expand the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile, Rep. Calvin Dooley said Tuesday.

"I'm anxious for the president to send up to (Congress) a request for fast track extension. I would hope that Congress would act on that prior to the summer recess," the California Democrat told reporters after addressing the U.S. Agriculture Department's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum.

Fast track authority guarantees Congress will vote promptly on proposed trade pacts without making an alterations. The administration has not said when it will submit a fast track bill. There is concern Republican-sponsored bills would be too restrictive to win Democratic support.
Dooley said issues over Chilean trade restrictions on imports of U.S. fruit and chicken needed to be resolved.
The lawmaker said he wanted fast track authority for an extended period of time so negotiations could be ongoing with Argentina, Venezuela, Brazil "or whoever else that we could interest."

He said the regional trading bloc Mercosur was a "real threat" to the U.S. ability to incorporate other Latin American countries into NAFTA, saying the longer it was in place the less incentive there would be for those nations to join NAFTA.
